title: Dermatomyositis dysphagia: perifascicular atrophy of striated (proximal esophageal) muscle
vignette: A 46-year-old woman comes to the office due to dysphagia. The patient has had difficulty swallowing both liquids and solid foods as well as frequent episodes of regurgitation and cough while eating. She has also had weakness in her extremities and a rash. The patient has no prior medical problems and takes no medications. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows an erythematous eruption on the upper eyelids. The oropharynx is clear and cardiopulmonary and abdominal examinations are unremarkable. She has difficulty lifting her arms above her head and standing from a sitting position. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's dysphagia?

clues.text: difficulty swallowing both liquids and solid foods
clues.note: Dysphagia to BOTH liquids and solids (plus regurgitation/cough while eating) suggests an oropharyngeal/upper-esophageal muscular problem rather than a mechanical obstruction.

clues.text: weakness in her extremities and a rash
clues.note: Proximal muscle weakness plus a rash is the classic combination of an inflammatory myopathy with skin involvement - dermatomyositis.

clues.text: erythematous eruption on the upper eyelids
clues.note: A heliotrope (violaceous) rash on the upper eyelids is characteristic of DERMATOMYOSITIS.

clues.text: difficulty lifting her arms above her head and standing from a sitting position
clues.note: Symmetric PROXIMAL muscle weakness (shoulders/hips) is the hallmark of dermatomyositis/polymyositis.

whatMatters: Heliotrope rash + proximal muscle weakness = DERMATOMYOSITIS, which attacks STRIATED (skeletal) muscle. The oropharynx and UPPER esophagus contain striated muscle, so the dysphagia results from PERIFASCICULAR ATROPHY of muscle fibers in the proximal esophageal muscularis. Answer E.
strategy: Recognize dermatomyositis (heliotrope rash + proximal weakness), then recall that its inflammation causes PERIFASCICULAR ATROPHY of STRIATED muscle - including the striated muscle of the oropharynx/upper esophagus -> dysphagia. Reject scleroderma (distal SMOOTH-muscle fibrosis - sclerodactyly/calcinosis, not heliotrope rash), eosinophilic esophagitis (mucosal eosinophils, food impaction), achalasia (myenteric plexus loss), and Zenker diverticulum (hypopharyngeal outpouching).

options.text: Atrophy and fibrous replacement of the distal esophageal muscularis propria
Diffuse eosinophil-predominant inflammation of the esophageal mucosa
Inflammation and degeneration of the esophageal myenteric plexus
Outpouching of hypopharyngeal mucosa through weakened muscle
Perifascicular atrophy of muscle fibers in the proximal esophageal muscularis propria

eliminations.label: Distal smooth-muscle fibrosis - scleroderma
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: atrophy/fibrous replacement of the DISTAL esophageal SMOOTH muscle (systemic sclerosis). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: scleroderma presents with sclerodactyly, digital ulcers, and calcinosis - not a heliotrope rash and proximal weakness; it affects the lower (smooth-muscle) esophagus. ✅ Correct if: reflux/dysphagia with scleroderma skin findings.

eliminations.label: Eosinophilic esophagitis - mucosal eosinophils
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: eosinophil-predominant mucosal inflammation (EoE). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: EoE causes dysphagia and food impaction with atopy, not proximal muscle weakness and a heliotrope rash. ✅ Correct if: dysphagia/impaction with rings ('trachealization') and mucosal eosinophils.

eliminations.label: Myenteric plexus loss - achalasia
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: degeneration of the esophageal myenteric (inhibitory) plexus (achalasia). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: achalasia causes impaired LES relaxation (bird-beak, smooth-muscle dysmotility), not a striated-muscle myopathy with skin disease. ✅ Correct if: dysphagia with failure of LES relaxation.

eliminations.label: Hypopharyngeal outpouching - Zenker diverticulum
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: herniation of hypopharyngeal mucosa through the cricopharyngeus (Zenker). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: Zenker causes dysphagia, regurgitation, and halitosis but is not associated with rash or proximal muscle weakness. ✅ Correct if: older patient with regurgitation of undigested food and a neck mass.

reasoning: Heliotrope rash + symmetric proximal muscle weakness = dermatomyositis
Dermatomyositis is an inflammatory myopathy of STRIATED (skeletal) muscle
The oropharynx and upper esophagus contain striated muscle -> perifascicular atrophy causes dysphagia
-> perifascicular atrophy of the proximal esophageal muscularis; answer E
mechanism: DERMATOMYOSITIS is an inflammatory myopathy that primarily affects STRIATED (skeletal) muscle and the skin. It presents with symmetric PROXIMAL muscle weakness (difficulty lifting the arms, rising from a chair) and characteristic skin findings - the HELIOTROPE (violaceous) eyelid rash and Gottron papules. Muscle biopsy classically shows PERIMYSIAL inflammation with PERIFASCICULAR ATROPHY (atrophy of fibers at the periphery of fascicles). Because the OROPHARYNX and UPPER (proximal) ESOPHAGUS contain STRIATED muscle, this myopathy involves them too, producing oropharyngeal DYSPHAGIA to both liquids and solids, regurgitation, and a risk of aspiration. Thus the dysphagia is due to perifascicular atrophy of muscle fibers in the proximal esophageal muscularis. This contrasts with SCLERODERMA, which fibroses the DISTAL SMOOTH muscle of the esophagus (reflux, with sclerodactyly/calcinosis rather than heliotrope rash). Other distractors are eosinophilic esophagitis (mucosal eosinophils), achalasia (myenteric plexus loss), and Zenker diverticulum (hypopharyngeal outpouching).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Rheum/GI > dermatomyositis: proximal muscle weakness + heliotrope rash/Gottron papules; perifascicular atrophy; affects striated muscle of oropharynx/upper esophagus (dysphagia); anti-Jo-1/anti-Mi-2; malignancy association.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Dermatomyositis attacks striated muscle; the upper esophagus is striated -> perifascicular atrophy -> dysphagia.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on dermatomyositis, heliotrope rash, perifascicular atrophy, striated vs smooth muscle, or oropharyngeal dysphagia? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Scleroderma = distal SMOOTH-muscle fibrosis (sclerodactyly); EoE = mucosal eosinophils; achalasia = myenteric plexus; Zenker = outpouching.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: dermatomyositis dysphagia = striated (upper esophageal) muscle involvement with perifascicular atrophy.

keywords.back: Involves striated muscle of oropharynx/upper esophagus

firstAid.detail: Rheum: striated-muscle myopathy; upper-esophageal perifascicular atrophy -> dysphagia.
GI > scleroderma, EoE, achalasia, Zenker differ.

memoryHook: Dermatomyositis inflames striped (striated) muscle - and the top of the swallowing tube is striated - so the same disease that lifts the arms weakly also weakens the upper esophagus (dysphagia).
